sampling_model.units: For each \(Q\in\mathcal Q_T\), independent and identically distributed primitive rows with law \(P_{\xi,Q}\) and one latent dense Gaussian interaction matrix induce the finite-array law \(P_{N,Q}\) over a fixed horizon.
sampling_model.treatment: Randomized independently across units and dates and entering \(g_{\beta_0}\).
sampling_model.overlap: The fixed constant \(\eta>0\) bounds all assignment probabilities.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(\beta_0\) from mean moments, \(\sigma^2\) and \(\tau^2\) from the energy regression, the full \(K\) from fitted messages, and the initial law by its empirical distribution. Uniform claims range only over admissible compact \(\mathcal K\) with the common constants in \(\text{def:compact-regular-family}\).

body.tldr: A fixed-horizon randomized experiment under homogeneous Causal-MP has a root-\(N\) fluctuation state evolution even though one unobserved Gaussian interaction matrix is reused at every date. An exact finite-\(N\) bridge conditions on the full observed past and uses empirical Gram projections to couple the reused-matrix fields to the auxiliary Gaussian-residual recursion. The theorem is uniform over an explicitly typed compact family \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal Q_T\) under named common moment, identification, rank, overlap, Gram, and Schur-residual margins. A single joint Gaussian experiment combines the differentiated mean, energy, Gram, and score moments with the initial-row empirical process. Its structural loading gives a direct asymptotic-linear representation for the all-treated-minus-none-treated path, and observable row contributions estimate the same covariance used by simultaneous Gaussian-max bands.

project_justification.gap: Causal-MP supplies first-order state evolution, consistent total-treatment-effect estimation, and heuristic intervals, but no root-\(N\) law for empirical means, second moments, or scores under reuse of one latent matrix.
project_justification.niche: Order-\(N^{-1/2}\) common-disorder terms are discarded by first-order laws and cannot be recovered by treating panel rows as independent.
project_justification.fill: Establish the finite-\(N\) conditional bridge with empirical Gram coefficients, construct the ordered auxiliary recursion and its ordinary derivative on the all-active interior, prove the expansion uniformly on compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal Q_T\), derive one joint moment--initial-law Gaussian experiment, map it through the structural and counterfactual derivatives, and calibrate an observable simultaneous path band from plug-in estimates of the same row influence.

body.related_work: Shirani and Bayati (2024, published Section 3, Theorems 1--2) establish first-order state evolution and consistency; their published Section 2.5 labels confidence-interval analysis heuristic. Bayati, Luo, Overman, Shirani, and Xiong (2024, Sections 2--4 and Algorithm 1) learn higher-order state-evolution update functions from observed mean, variance, treatment, and nonlinear features and discuss empirical intervals or replicated error bars, but they do not prove the proposed analytic root-\(N\) joint covariance, feasible influence covariance, or simultaneous coverage law. Bayati and Montanari (2011) supply adaptive Gaussian conditioning for AMP with an Onsager correction; the relevant distinction is the exact finite-\(N\) full-past bridge with empirical Gram coefficients for a reused nonsymmetric matrix and no Onsager correction. Rush and Venkataramanan (2018) establish finite-sample concentration, and Bao, Han, and Xu (2025) establish leave-one-out representations; these papers inform the projection and remainder arguments without claiming the aggregate causal fluctuation law. Qiu, Sun, and Zhou (2024) study multiple derived causal outcomes, while Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013) supply Gaussian-max calibration after asymptotic linearity. Wang, Zhong, and Fan (2024) and Gueddari, Hachem, and Najim (2025) concern broader first-order AMP laws rather than centered Causal-MP covariance.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The target is the deterministic population-limit path, not a realized finite-network counterfactual path. The theory is fixed-\(T\), Gaussian-interaction, and confined to compact regular families \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal Q_T\) with the named common envelope, chart, identification, rank, overlap, Gram, and Schur-residual constants in \(\text{def:compact-regular-family}\). Rank-changing laws and exact zero-pivot laws are excluded boundary cases; no continuity or differentiability is claimed there. In \(\text{def:rank-boundary-perturbation}\), \(U_{i1}^{(\delta)}=U_{i0}+\delta V_i\) gives residual energy \(\delta^2\) and field \(H_{i0}+|\delta|Z_{i1}^{\circ}\), so the two-sided derivative fails at the redundant-message boundary. Weak energy designs, variance boundaries, fixed positive ridge, model selection, and growing horizons require separate limits.
body.honest_scope: The finite-\(N\) Gaussian bridge uses the conditioning fields \(\mathscr F_{N,t}\) and empirical coefficients \(K^N,\lambda_t^N,\rho_t^N\); the open content is the uniformly root-\(N\) row-averaged linearization on each admissible compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal Q_T\), where \(Q\) induces both \(P_{\xi,Q}\) and \(P_{N,Q}\). The topology \(\mathcal T_{\mathcal E}\) combines envelope-weighted weak convergence of primitive-row laws with Euclidean convergence of finite-dimensional parameters. The common constants \(\delta_{\mathrm{mom}},B_{\mathcal E},\varepsilon_{\mathcal B},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id}},c_{\mathrm{id}},\underline j,\underline x,\eta,\underline\kappa,\underline\rho\) control moments, chart distance, identification, the two rank conditions, overlap, Gram blocks, and Schur residuals. The empirical law remains in the same all-active open neighborhood uniformly, and derivatives use the ordinary ambient empirical-process tangent space. Rank-changing and exact zero-pivot laws remain outside the theorem. The single experiment \(\mathbb Z_T^{\mathrm{full}}\) contains the complete moment vector and initial-row empirical process; the path influence is \(D\Psi_T[\zeta_T(\xi)]\), so \(\Omega_\theta\) and \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\) refer to the same row-level object. The counterfactual first transition integrates under \(P_{0X}\), and Gaussian integration begins only after the dense interaction creates the Gaussian state. In the affine \(T=3\) reduction, the checked table gives \(q=(1/2,85/64,159/128)\), \(K_{01}=7/32\), \(\det(X_v^{\top}X_v)=10191/8192\), consecutive mean covariance \(19/16\), reuse component \(7/32\), and causal path \((1,3/2,7/4)\). At \(T=1\), the influence recursion reduces to the ordinary empirical initial-row fluctuation plus the Gaussian structural residual.
